data.narrative:
Stellaria is a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Nicolas Breyton and backed by CEA and Schneider Electric. It has raised €23M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 nuclear energy companies: three public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and eight private firms including Nano Nuclear Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using the €23M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of €58M. The peer-median method is not applicable; while six same-sector peers exist, insufficient datapoints meet narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier), and relying on all-sector medians would introduce unwarranted noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €49M to €66M, with a median of €58M. This narrow range reflects dependence on a single method. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for the nuclear energy sector specifically, limited visibility into comparable seed-stage nuclear transactions, and the degree to which Stellaria's institutional backing (CEA, Schneider Electric) commands a premium or discount relative to other early-stage entrants. Additional data on recent seed rounds within the narrow nuclear energy cohort would materially strengthen confidence in this range.
